all_current_citation_contexts.context_text: Schema information ranges from source ontologies to application-maintained configurations and discovered instance patterns. The /facet browser computes schema and property closures around its repository \citep{2006_Hildebrand_facet_A}. Sparklis discovers endpoint structure without requiring prior schema preprocessing \citep{2017_Ferre_Sparklis_An}. ViziQuer uses schema and resource information for contextual completion; the DBpedia report describes indexed context and explicit query restrictions \citep{V3-01013}. Sampo-UI provides reusable components while still requiring domain perspectives and query configuration \citep{2022_Ikkala_Sampo-UI_A}. ``Generic'' can therefore mean portability of software, automatic discovery, or freedom from domain-specific design; these are different claims.

nominated_pair.nominated_fact_paraphrase: Connecting relationships found through SPARQL searches

manuscript_context.context_text: RelFinder makes the relationship itself the search object. Users select entities, disambiguate labels, and inspect directed paths obtained through iterative SPARQL searches \citep{2009_Heim_RelFinder_Revealing}. Path length, direction, and search bounds determine which relationships appear. This is distinct from simply expanding neighboring nodes: a path-search interface must communicate its search scope and the meaning of an absent path. Computed association graphs also require explicit semantics. Semantic Wonder Cloud combines exploration with similarity-based connections; these connections must be interpreted as computed relationships rather than automatically as assertions present in DBpedia \citep{V3-02469}.

all_current_citation_contexts.context_text: Numeric evidence must retain its workload. The FAAS timing experiment covers 268 property-autocompletion requests: four join templates combined with 67 weighted-sampled Wikidata properties, completing the property variable \texttt{?q}. All FAAS requests completed within three seconds, while 36\% of WDQS requests completed within the endpoint timeout. The local index used the 23 May 2020 Wikidata truthy dump, filtered to 1.098 billion triples. Preprocessing took 75 hours and produced a 9.7-GB index on an i7-4600M CPU at 2.9 GHz with 16 GB RAM and Windows 10 \citep{2021_Parra_Fast_Approximate}. The timing workload covers all 268 requests; the reported median precision of 0.21 concerns only requests for which WDQS returned results. Neither quantity measures complete human task time. Graph-Query Suggestions reports average retrieval/query-answering below one second and millisecond scoring over a 76-million-node, 314-million-edge graph; these are component times, not complete human task durations \citep{2020_Lissandrini_Graph-Query_Suggestions}. FeedLens reports a twelve-fold speedup for a separate offline summary-embedding experiment, whose integration was future work in the assessed interface \citep{V3-01126}.

all_current_citation_contexts.context_text: RQ2 concerns the contract between a suggestion and the action it invites. An application should state whether a candidate is schema-compatible, observed in data, approximate, or ranked by relevance. It should distinguish a guaranteed executable step from a potentially useful extension. The low precision of approximate autocompletion and the weak single-exemplar ranking result make this distinction concrete \citep{2021_Parra_Fast_Approximate,2020_Lissandrini_Graph-Query_Suggestions}. Users need the ability to inspect the reason for a suggestion and undo its effect without losing their prior state.

all_current_citation_contexts.context_text: \citet{V3-00696} combine topic classification, hierarchical paper clusters, and grounded comparisons of scholarly publications in a conversational interface over a Neo4j knowledge graph. Their forty-participant comparison counterbalances interface order between two groups, while scenario order remains fixed. Mean SUS scores for the conversational and graphical interfaces are 76.00 and 77.25 in the first scenario, and 76.63 and 65.25 in the second. The report presents descriptive ratings without a significance test or objective retrieval/time gain. Participants also reported difficulties with backtracking and with choosing between buttons and free text. The example connects generated guidance with a constrained task flow; it does not establish unrestricted conversation or a benefit across domains.

evaluation_units_and_unknowns_preserved.design: Three distinct evaluations: offline research-topic classification; abstract-sentence classification with qualitative manual inspection of comparisons; and a two-group counterbalanced human comparison. For the human study participants were randomly assigned to Groups A/B with similar demographic distributions. Group A used conversational Scenario 1 then graphical Scenario 2; Group B used graphical Scenario 1 then conversational Scenario 2. Each person used both interfaces on different scenarios; scenario order was fixed in the described sequence.
evaluation_units_and_unknowns_preserved.participants: Human study: 40 recruited participants, Group A n=20 and Group B n=20; Table 3 reports 40 overall participants. Recruited through university courses/social networks; basic technical knowledge and English proficiency, interest in NLP, target non-experts. Ages 20–29, mean 25.03; 14 female and 26 male. Separate component samples: 1,601 synthetic training questions and 364 test questions for topic classification; 500 computer-science abstracts / 3,287 labelled sentences for SciBERT. Two researchers manually assessed generated comparisons. Outcome-specific analytic sample sizes and attrition/completion counts are not separately reported.
evaluation_units_and_unknowns_preserved.tasks: Human exploratory search: find publications on (1) NLP analysis of mental-health/emotion expressions on social media during COVID-19, and (2) automatic generation of multiple-choice exams for a Python programming course. Main method allows approximately 10 minutes per interface; Appendix Table 2 says up to 8 minutes and encourages thinking aloud. Component tasks classify search goals into NLP topics and abstract sentences into rhetorical categories; these are separate from human retrieval tasks.
evaluation_units_and_unknowns_preserved.comparators: Human study compares the conversational scholarly-search interface with the ACL Anthology graphical interface using traditional text search. Topic classification compares SPECTER2-based vector similarity, GPT-3.5-Turbo prompting and a SetFit classifier. Abstract-sentence classification reports a comparison with the prior Gonçalves et al. model; manual comparison-summary assessment is qualitative.
evaluation_units_and_unknowns_preserved.measures: Human study: System Usability Scale (SUS; 0–100), five-point ratings of perceived readability, correctness, usefulness, generated-comparison quality and overall satisfaction, plus two free-text feedback fields. Topic classification: accuracy and macro F1; abstract-sentence classification: reported F1. Human perceived correctness is not an objective retrieval-accuracy score.
evaluation_units_and_unknowns_preserved.results: Human Table 1: SUS conversational/graphical mean (SD) = 76.00 (18.94)/77.25 (15.28) for Scenario 1 and 76.63 (16.63)/65.25 (23.91) for Scenario 2. Readability, perceived correctness, usefulness and satisfaction means favor the conversational interface in both scenarios; summary quality was rated only for the conversational interface. Descriptive ratings and qualitative feedback are reported without an inferential significance or effect-size test. Separate topic-classifier macro F1: vector search below 0.50, prompting near 0.75, SetFit 0.95. Separate SciBERT abstract-sentence F1: 75.39% versus 74.60% in the cited prior model.
evaluation_units_and_unknowns_preserved.limitations: The sample is narrow (40 participants aged 20–29, university/social-network recruitment) and tasks are two predefined scholarly-NLP scenarios. Each participant uses a given scenario with one interface only; interface assignment/order is counterbalanced while described scenario order stays Scenario 1 then Scenario 2. No outcome-specific analytic N, attrition, objective human retrieval-accuracy score, task-time improvement, inferential significance test, confidence interval or standardized effect size is reported. Preserve the approximately-10-minute versus up-to-8-minute timing inconsistency. Reported interaction problems include difficulty learning the three-phase flow, unclear buttons versus free text, and backtracking. Component scores concern synthetic topic questions / abstract-sentence classification, not human search effectiveness.

all_current_citation_contexts.context_text: Schema information ranges from source ontologies to application-maintained configurations and discovered instance patterns. The /facet browser computes schema and property closures around its repository \citep{2006_Hildebrand_facet_A}. Sparklis discovers endpoint structure without requiring prior schema preprocessing \citep{2017_Ferre_Sparklis_An}. ViziQuer uses schema and resource information for contextual completion; the DBpedia report describes indexed context and explicit query restrictions \citep{V3-01013}. Sampo-UI provides reusable components while still requiring domain perspectives and query configuration \citep{2022_Ikkala_Sampo-UI_A}. ``Generic'' can therefore mean portability of software, automatic discovery, or freedom from domain-specific design; these are different claims.

The Linked Data browser with recommendations uses user interaction to guide subsequent resources \citep{2018_Durao_A_Linked}. all_current_citation_contexts.context_text: Numeric evidence must retain its workload. The FAAS timing experiment covers 268 property-autocompletion requests: four join templates combined with 67 weighted-sampled Wikidata properties, completing the property variable \texttt{?q}. All FAAS requests completed within three seconds, while 36\% of WDQS requests completed within the endpoint timeout. The local index used the 23 May 2020 Wikidata truthy dump, filtered to 1.098 billion triples. Preprocessing took 75 hours and produced a 9.7-GB index on an i7-4600M CPU at 2.9 GHz with 16 GB RAM and Windows 10 \citep{2021_Parra_Fast_Approximate}. The timing workload covers all 268 requests; the reported median precision of 0.21 concerns only requests for which WDQS returned results. Neither quantity measures complete human task time. Graph-Query Suggestions reports average retrieval/query-answering below one second and millisecond scoring over a 76-million-node, 314-million-edge graph; these are component times, not complete human task durations \citep{2020_Lissandrini_Graph-Query_Suggestions}. FeedLens reports a twelve-fold speedup for a separate offline summary-embedding experiment, whose integration was future work in the assessed interface \citep{V3-01126}.

all_current_citation_contexts.context_text: For RQ4, the reported evidence supports different, bounded conclusions. Usability ratings and qualitative observations describe experience in particular tasks and samples. Comparative studies can reveal tradeoffs: FeedLens reports a higher mean SUS score and longer task duration than its baseline, while RDF Surveyor reports experience-dependent ratings without a randomized comparator \citep{V3-01126,V3-01765}. Query-interpretation and construction exercises, offline ranking, and execution benchmarks measure different outcomes; their results do not establish a common cross-system effectiveness estimate. Future trials should state participant expertise, domain familiarity, training, task materials, allocation, task order, and comparator version. Correctness and time can be combined with qualitative observation when their definitions are clear. Discovery tasks also need criteria for the usefulness, novelty, and evidential support of findings. Component benchmarks should separate network retrieval, ranking, query execution, transfer, and rendering, with data size and hardware. A large source graph is not sufficient evidence of scalable interaction.

all_current_citation_contexts.context_text: User expertise should guide the amount and timing of control. A domain specialist may know which entities matter while being unfamiliar with query joins; a technical user may understand SPARQL while lacking domain vocabulary. The medical studies and RDF Surveyor experience differences show that these dimensions should be measured separately \citep{2021_Witschel_Natural_Language-based,2022_Grether_Studying_Interaction,V3-01765}. Progressive controls can begin with meaningful examples and valid refinements, then expose relationship direction, query scope, and advanced constructs. This is a design implication from observed problems and supported mechanisms, not an established cross-system effect size.

all_current_citation_contexts.context_text: For RQ4, the reported evidence supports different, bounded conclusions. Usability ratings and qualitative observations describe experience in particular tasks and samples. Comparative studies can reveal tradeoffs: FeedLens reports a higher mean SUS score and longer task duration than its baseline, while RDF Surveyor reports experience-dependent ratings without a randomized comparator \citep{V3-01126,V3-01765}. Query-interpretation and construction exercises, offline ranking, and execution benchmarks measure different outcomes; their results do not establish a common cross-system effectiveness estimate. Future trials should state participant expertise, domain familiarity, training, task materials, allocation, task order, and comparator version. Correctness and time can be combined with qualitative observation when their definitions are clear. Discovery tasks also need criteria for the usefulness, novelty, and evidential support of findings. Component benchmarks should separate network retrieval, ranking, query execution, transfer, and rendering, with data size and hardware. A large source graph is not sufficient evidence of scalable interaction.

manuscript_context.context_text: RelFinder makes the relationship itself the search object. Users select entities, disambiguate labels, and inspect directed paths obtained through iterative SPARQL searches \citep{2009_Heim_RelFinder_Revealing}. Path length, direction, and search bounds determine which relationships appear. This is distinct from simply expanding neighboring nodes: a path-search interface must communicate its search scope and the meaning of an absent path. Computed association graphs also require explicit semantics. Semantic Wonder Cloud combines exploration with similarity-based connections; these connections must be interpreted as computed relationships rather than automatically as assertions present in DBpedia \citep{V3-02469}.
